quotes.text: A workload identity is different. It's a digital badge for software. That software could be an app your team built an automation that runs on a schedule, a background service, or even an AI agent
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Simple definition of a workload identity with concrete examples.

quotes.text: So when you hear these names keep this map in your head, the application registration is the app's master design. The service principle is its working identity inside your company.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Untangles two commonly confused Entra terms.

quotes.text: But an identity alone doesn't grant access. The logic app still needs a role or permission. Someone must allow that identity to read the required secret, use the required API or reach the required resource.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the common misconception that a managed identity grants access by itself.

quotes.text: That's why a client secret deserves the same care as a powerful password, and why it should be the last choice when a better sign-in method exists.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear security recommendation on client secrets.

quotes.text: Every workload identity needs a named owner. That owner should know why it exists, what it can access, how it signs in, and when somebody will review it again.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable governance rule for workload identities.

takeaways: Workload identities give applications, automations and AI agents their own Entra identity instead of shared service accounts or passwords in code.

An application registration is the app's global design, a service principal is its local identity in each tenant, and a managed identity is a service principal that Azure manages for an Azure resource.
Prefer managed identities inside Azure and workload identity federation outside it, use certificates over client secrets, grant minimal permissions and give every workload identity an owner.
hook: Apps, pipelines and AI agents need access too, yet many still hide passwords in code and config files. In this Simply Explained episode, Mirko Peters gives Azure admins, developers and architects a plain-English map of Microsoft Entra workload identities, managed identities, service principals and federation, plus a practical checklist for securing them.
